title: The 10am NQ strategy everyone is backtesting did -3.7% over the window the Nasdaq nearly doubled in
author: person-person12
selftext:
A guru named Powell has a 10am NQ strategy that has been all over my feed for months, and the thing i never see posted beside those results is what just holding the index did over the same window.

So i ran it. The rules got built and replayed over 1 minute NQ candles from july 2023 to feb 2026 in [Agenticks](https://www.agenticks.ca/?utm_source=reddit&utm_medium=post&utm_campaign=autopilot&utm_content=ai_trading), 100k account, one contract, every trade logged.

**535 trades. 60.2% win rate. Profit factor 0.98. Net -$3,675.** Max drawdown 25.55%, average win $522, average loss $806.

It wins 6 out of every 10 trades and still loses money, because the losers run about 1.5x the size of the winners, which works out to roughly negative 7 dollars a trade.

Heres the part that actually matters though. Buy and hold on the same instrument over that same window took 100k to about 170k, and the strategy did -3.7%. So this isnt a system losing a bit of money in a flat market, **its one losing money through one of the strongest runs the Nasdaq has ever had.**

Split by condition it gets worse. 280 of the 535 trades happened in volatile conditions and those lost $6,764 at a 0.93 profit factor. The only regime it made money in was uptrends, 152 trades, 1.08 profit factor, +$3,307. So the edge is mostly the index going up, and it captured less of that than sitting still would have.

**\_\_\_\_\_**

What he teaches publicly is the shape of it, not a rulebook. Mark the 10am candle, wait for one side to get swept, wait for the move back through, take the continuation into first liquidity. Thats real, but first liquidity is something you read off a chart rather than a number, and there is no published stop, no cutoff time and no trade limit. So what got tested is the mechanical skeleton with sane defaults filled in, and two of those choices change what youre measuring. It only took longs where he trades both ways, and it entered on a plain break and retest instead of requiring the displacement leg.

Somebody running a tighter rulebook on it would get a different number. The 170k the index did across those same 31 months doesnt move either way.
